l.i: 32 Virum ens reale sit genus univocum entis

main_text.l: NON levis de hac quæstione inter Metaphysicos est
disceptatio. Sed brevitatis studio statuendum puto,
Ens reale non esse genus univocum, sed analogum. Non
enim æquo prædicatur de ente increato & creato, sed
secundum analogiam & modum prioris & posterioris.
Deus enim perfectissimo modo est ens reale primum,
quatenus à nullo pendet; omnia vero ab ipso: Deinde
quatenus ante omnia alia entia sunt; Hæc vero omnia
post ipsum: Tertio, quatenus est infinitæ essentiæ & vir-
tutis: Creaturæ vero sunt entia realia, quatenus certum
& limitatum: sendi[?] modum à Deo acceperunt, ac vnaquæque
cum eo aliquam similitudinem habet. Nec ob
stat, si quis obiiciar[?] inter infinitum & finitum nullam
esse proportionem: Ideoque ens reale non posse esse genus
analogum entis increati & creati. Licet enim inter in-
finitum & finitum nulla detur proportio mathematica,
datur tamen proportio seu analogia metaphysica, qua-
tenus in ratione entis quodam modo inter se conveni-
unt, infinitumque est principium, à quo omnia finita
entia suæ habent originem.

l.i: 13 An solus Deus sit ens primum & increatum?

main_text.l: S-
tatuitur thesis affirmativa. Rationes sunt: 1, Quia

αὐτύπαρκτος[?].
2, Quia nullum ens habet se prius.
3, Quia omnium entium est summum & perfectissimum.

page.notes: Partly visible note at the bottom left is cut off by the edge of the scan and could not be read. The symbol after the first marginal note is uncertain and was read as "&c.". Several words in the first line of the body text were uncertain and are not marked, including "brevitatis" (printed form may differ) and "sendi" (initial letter unclear). The sentence continues beyond this part of the page. The left margin numerals I. to V. and the labels Obiectio, Responsio and Prothesis are printed in the margin and are kept as notes. The Greek in the first thesis paragraph is uncertain and is marked with [?] or illegible. The word "obiiciar" may be a printing error for "obiiciat". The Greek numeral line "I." is set as its own paragraph.
